content: Kinetic networks carry mechanical power: RPM (speed) and torque (twisting force). Power in watts is torque times angular velocity.
Sources (generators) push power; shafts carry it; gears and gearboxes trade speed for torque; clutches engage and disengage branches.
Every consumer demands a minimum RPM and torque. Deliver less and the machine browns out — it runs slower, proportionally, instead of stopping.
Overload the network and everything on it suffers. Build transmission deliberately: the Processor will demand it.
title: Kinetic Systems
